events.text: You have noticed it for years without a word for it: what you learn stays learned, and each new realm stops feeling new sooner than anyone said it would. Tonight, sitting still, you feel it go all the way down. Something in your bones finishes a long settling, the way a house finishes creaking after the last of the winter.

choices.text: Sit with it until dawn

effects.log: Nothing happens, for hours, and it is the most useful night of your life. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Get up and test it on the practice post

effects.log: The post splits on the third blow and your hands do not sting. Your body wakes.

events.text: At Peak Master the body heaven gave you stops being a gift and becomes a door. One morning the clouds over your roof part by themselves, and a column of light comes down and stands in the yard, waiting, the way a servant waits for a guest to go in first.

choices.text: Walk into the light slowly, and learn what it is

effects.log: It takes all day. By evening you understand that heaven was never your teacher: it was your sparring partner, and it has been holding back. Your body wakes. (Training and power rise; the Heaven-Born Rhythm strikes harder.)

choices.text: Run into it with everything you have

ok.log: The light goes through you like a bell through a valley. Half the province sees the pillar. Your body wakes, all at once.

fail.log: The light knocks you flat for a week. When you get up, the body is awake anyway, and slightly offended.

events.text: The cold you were born with has waited your whole life for this. At Peak Master it rises all at once: frost on the inside of your windows, ice in your teacup at midsummer, a ring of white spreading across the floor from where you sit. It is not trying to kill you. It is trying to become you.

choices.text: Let the cold in. All of it

effects.log: For three days you cannot feel your hands. On the fourth the cold settles, and your qi moves like a river under ice: silent, and much faster than it looks. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Hold the cold at the dantian and let it out a thread at a time

ok.log: A thread at a time, for a whole winter. The cold learns your rhythm, and you learn its. Your body wakes, under control.

fail.log: The thread becomes a flood. You wake in a block of frost the size of a coffin, alive, and awake in every sense.

events.text: The fire in your meridians has always run hot. At Peak Master it stops running and starts roaring: the water in your bath boils, paper curls when you read it, and the sect's physicians will not take your pulse without wet cloths. The furnace is open. The question is what you feed it.

choices.text: Feed it your training, year on year

effects.log: You train in the snow for a season, and the snow does not stay. When the fire finally settles, it settles as strength. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Feed it all at once, in one great burn

ok.log: One night, one burn, one pillar of fire on the mountainside that the villages talk about for years. Your body wakes, roaring.

fail.log: The burn goes too deep and takes a little of your years with it. But the furnace is open now, and it is yours.

events.text: At Peak Master the body you were born with finally says what it wants. You dream of blood moons and wake with your hands already in the demonic forms. Every cultist within a hundred li looks up from what they are doing at the same moment, and nobody knows why.

choices.text: Give the body what it wants

effects.log: You stop fighting it. It is the strongest you have ever felt, and the darkest. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Master it: you are the one who decides

ok.log: A month of nights fighting yourself, and you win. The demon body wakes, and it wakes as yours.

fail.log: You win most of the nights. Not all. The body wakes, and something of the demon wakes with it.

events.text: At Peak Master the deep, still energy that gathered in you for so long finally fills. You sit by a lake one night and the lake goes perfectly flat, and stays flat, and the moon in it is clearer than the moon in the sky.

choices.text: Sit until the moon sets, and listen

effects.log: You hear the water think. By dawn you are sure it heard you too. Your body wakes, as quietly as water.

choices.text: Play the qin to the still water

ok.log: Every note goes into the lake and does not come back. Fishermen on the far shore weep and do not know why. Your body wakes.

fail.log: A string breaks at the third note. The lake ripples, once, as if laughing. The body wakes anyway.

events.text: At Peak Master, one morning, every sword in the city hums at once. Smiths drop their hammers. A sect's whole armoury rattles in its racks. All of them lean, very slightly, toward the street where you are buying breakfast.

choices.text: Draw your own sword and answer them

effects.log: One clean stroke in the empty street, and the humming stops, as if they had been waiting for permission. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Go to the old battlefield where a thousand swords are buried

ok.log: You walk among the planted blades for a day and a night. Every one of them tells you how it was broken. Your body wakes, and your sword is the better for it.

fail.log: An old blade cuts you as you pass, not quite by accident. The bones wake anyway, with a lesson in them.

events.text: At Peak Master the cold in your body turns to jade. You sit under a pine in a snowstorm and the snow falls all round you and does not touch you once. An old woodcutter watches the whole afternoon and goes home and tells his family he has seen an immortal.

choices.text: Stay in the storm until it ends

effects.log: Three days. When the storm ends you are exactly as warm as when it began. Your body wakes, and the years slow again.

choices.text: Walk through the storm to the top of the mountain

ok.log: At the summit the wind is a wall. You walk through it. Your body wakes like the first frost: everywhere at once.

fail.log: The mountain wins this time. The body wakes on the way down, which is almost the same thing.

events.text: It took longer for you than for anyone: the Five Elements body fills slowly. But at Peak Master the phases turn once, all the way round, for the first time. Wood feeds fire, fire makes earth, earth bears metal, metal carries water, water feeds wood. Something that was five things becomes one.

choices.text: Follow the cycle with your breath until it is yours

effects.log: A month of breathing round and round the five phases. When it ends nothing in you can be pushed out of balance: not a blow, not a gate, not your own qi. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Turn it the other way: the cycle that destroys

ok.log: Water quenches fire, fire melts metal, metal cuts wood. You learn the cycle of overcoming as well as the one of making. Your body wakes, and it knows how to break things now.

fail.log: The destroying cycle is not kind to beginners. But the phases hold each other, as they always will, and the body wakes.

events.text: The body you exchanged for was never born in anyone. It is still settling into you, the way a river settles into a new bed. One night it settles all the way, and for a moment you remember what it was like before there was a heaven or an earth to tell apart.

choices.text: Hold on to the memory

effects.log: It goes, as such memories go. What it leaves is a body that does not quite believe in limits. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Let it go, and keep only the feeling

effects.log: You let it go. The feeling stays: that every gate is a door somebody painted on a wall. Your body wakes.

events.text: An old physician takes your pulse, lets go as if it burned, and sits down. "Your body will eat your years," he says. "I have read of one cure. Somewhere in the murim there is a person born with the opposite body, and the same short life. If the two of you meet and trade qi, palm to palm, both curses break. If you never meet, both of you die young."
events.arc: The Meeting of Yin and Yang

choices.text: Ask where to look

effects.log: "Where the opposite would be," he says, unhelpfully, and then, more helpfully: "The cold ones go north. The hot ones go to the deserts. Start there."

choices.text: Laugh it off. Short and bright is fine

effects.log: You thank him and pay him and do not think about it. Mostly.

events.text: You find {npc} in an inn at the far edge of the empire: thin, too bright, the same short life written in the skin. {He} knows what you are the moment you walk in, the way a flame knows water. "I heard someone was looking," {he} says. "I did not believe it."
events.arc: The Meeting of Yin and Yang

choices.text: Put your palm against {his}. Now, before either of you thinks better of it

ok.log: Cold meets fire through two palms, and for an hour the inn steams like a bathhouse. When it ends, you both breathe like ordinary people for the first time in your lives. The curse is broken. (+30 years)

fail.log: Too fast. The qi crashes instead of meeting, and you are both thrown across the room. Something has shifted, a little. Not enough. You agree to try again, slower.

choices.text: Sit with {him} first. Talk. Learn the shape of {his} qi

effects.log: You talk until dawn about cold and fire and how it feels to count your years. When you finally try, you will know exactly how {he} breathes.

events.text: Some time later, on a quiet mountain, you and {npc} try again: slowly this time, breath by breath, the way you planned it. Cold goes one way and fire the other, and somewhere between your palms they meet and do not fight.
events.arc: The Meeting of Yin and Yang

choices.text: Hold on until it is finished

effects.log: It takes a night and a day. At the end, the two of you are just two tired people on a mountain, with all your years ahead of you. The curse is broken. (+30 years)

choices.text: Give {him} more than half, so {he} is cured for certain

effects.log: You push more of your qi across than you keep. {He} notices, and does not say anything for a long time. Both curses break, {his} a little more cleanly than yours. (+24 years)
